fitzgen opened PR #15034 from fitzgen:lazy-lenders to bytecodealliance:main:

This commit introduces a lazy_lenders buffer on VMStoreContext. When we need to push a lender for a resource borrow, but haven't forced the lazy thread context yet, we push to lazy_landers. This avoids forcing the lazy thread context, like we previously did. Each VMDeferredThread keeps a watermark of the lazy_lenders length upon construction so that, when we do something that does force the lazy thread context, we can partition lazy_lenders by each thread context that is responsible for those borrows.

This does not change what is inlined in Wasm code or what is done in libcalls. In the inline exit-sync-call fast path, we bail out to the host when there are lazy lends to be undone. The host libcall still takes care to avoid forcing the VMDeferredThread right before we exit the call in this case.

Follow up commits will move a bunch of this work inline into the adapters, but I wanted to keep this introduction of lazy_lenders as small as I could.

Even so, this is a significant speedup for cm-online-stats, our adapter-call-heavy Sightglass benchmark:

:memo: cfallin submitted PR review:

Thanks! This rates as "plausible" to me only because I'm not deeply familiar with the borrow machinery here; @alexcrichton should probably look it over too. Just a few comments I noted below as I read through.

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

"Watermark" to me implies some sort of lazy "max seen so far" behavior; this is really just "start of our segment in lazy_lenders", right? So lazy_lenders_index or lazy_lenders_start might be more clear?

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

We could avoid the smallvec clone here with a hypothetical components_data.lazy_lenders_and_task_state_mut() returning a split borrow, perhaps (similar to the trick we play in a bunch of instances on StoreOpaque)?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

A few thoughts on this:

  • One possibly more-optimizable shape here would be to store the number of lazy lens per-frame rather than storing the current length before the frame in the frame. That way if nothing actually does a borrow then this never even looks at lazy_lenders_start.
  • Is band the right way to generate good clif here? I'd expect we'd have better codegen from two icmp + brif instructions as opposed to a band which'd require a bunch of seto and test and such. Perhaps arguably something to happen in ISLE too, but my guess is that our current codegen for brif(band(icmp(...), icmp(...))) is pretty bad

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Subjectively I'd say we could probably get away with a much smaller value here, even something like 4 or maybe 8. This seems relatively difficult to fill in conventional components where there's not all that much cross-component-talk and fast paths generally need just one or two slots.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

We talked about this briefly elsewhere, but personally I'd say just go ahead and remove this and inline the constant LAZY_LENDERS_CAPACITY everywhere since it seems pretty unlikely we'd want to double this at runtime.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Instead of a packed u64 would it make sense for this to be just two u32 fields, perhaps with the raw index type itself?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Would it make sense to back this up with a debug_assert!?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Instead of a LazyLendersFull error, could this perhaps return Option<..> where None means "no you can't push the capacity is full"

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

How come this is all #[cfg]'d to component-model-async? I'd naively expect the optimization here to equally apply with/without component-model-async

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Would it be possible to just delete this code? This seems like it'll all quickly become dead code as this would otherwise happen in cranelift-compiled code otherwise. I think it's reasonable to add the lazy infrastructure here, but I also think it'd be best to avoid adding pieces that won't survive to the final implementation (where possible)

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

This method is mostly a duplicate of what's below, in particular the let guest block and assembling all the borrows and such. Could these methods be combined to share more of the implementation?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Any particular reason to split out reserve/push here? OOM-wise I figure it doesn't really matter if we drop a borrow or two while we're trapping due to OOM

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

We talked a bit about this elsewhere, but I wanted to write this down here too. I think it'd be best to ideally remove the need for this method altogether where the lazy lend is a record of "here's the borrows we haven't yet accounted for in the official tables" and then undoing that is a simple "move the stack pointer" style operation which needs no sort of destructor or such. That would make actually recording a lazy lend that much faster (just put the resource in a table) and would keep everything consistent I believe as well.

I'm hopeful that something like this would help simplify both this PR as-is and subsequent PRs to add more infrastructure, but I could also be off-the-mark here

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

To keep raw values, maybe flip this and have the host at u32::MAX and other types as-is?

:thumbs_up: alexcrichton submitted PR review:

Overall lgtm, but the main thing that doesn't sit well with me still is all the #[cfg] necessary. When removing most of them I see locally that indeed promote_lazy_lends isn't used, but that also doesn't sit well with me. There's nothing component-model-async-specific about any of this code and it's, in theory at least, all equally applicable both with and without async.

My main worry is that we'll get ourselves into a situation where in certain compilation modes, which aren't well tested, we end up mismatching lazy things vs not. For example we would accidentally push lazy lends but then not actually ever flush the list or try promotion at some point. I don't believe that's currently happening, but all the configuration options we have put us precariously close to being in this situation.

Would you be ok with a tact like:

  • Filing an issue for using deferred tasks/threads without component-model-async at compile time
  • Removing all #[cfg] in this PR related to component-model-async
  • Adding #[cfg_attr(not(async), expect(dead_code, ...))] to the dead methods when component-model-async is disabled

My hope with that is to avoid undue #[cfg] traffic, keep track in-code that something isn't implemented yet, and have at least an issue on file for this. My attempt left a few assorted #[cfg(feature = "component-model")] annotations which I'd ideally like to see moved into component-specific locations as opposed to gating, but that's relatively minor. One example was impl VMResourceIndex which could probably move to vm/component.rs
